request: Analyze GSE263838 for PMID 38766755 (The interactive effect of sustained sleep restriction and resistance exercise on skeletal muscle transcriptomics in young females.): how exercise affects gene expression as the paper intends.

final.assay: bulk total RNA-seq (Ribo-Zero), vastus lateralis, Kallisto GRCh38 (S2.8.p1)
final.design: randomised cross-over: 10 resistance-trained females, normal sleep (NS) vs sleep restriction (SR), resistance exercise sessions on days 3,5,7,9; RNA-seq on PRE-exercise biopsies of day 3 and day 9 only (S2.2.p2, S2.7.p1, S3.2.p2)
final.repeated_measure_unit: participant (each woman sampled in both conditions and both days)
final.sample_inclusion: all RNA sequencing samples (S2.8.p1); 10 participants x 2 conditions x 2 days = 40 planned, 38 deposited
final.primary_estimand: exercise-training effect: pre-exercise day 9 (48 h after the 3rd of three REx sessions on days 3,5,7) vs pre-exercise day 3 (before any session in that condition), within NS and within SR (S3.2.p7); secondary: SR vs NS at day 3 and at day 9 (S3.2.p2)
planned_contrasts: NS day 9 vs NS day 3 (exercise training under normal sleep; paper: 2962 DEGs, up 128 / down 2834, S3.2.p7)
SR day 9 vs SR day 3 (exercise training under sleep restriction; paper: 2219 DEGs, up 102 / down 2117, S3.2.p7)
SR vs NS at day 3 (sleep restriction, no exercise; paper: 1 DEG, GGNBP2, S3.2.p2)
SR vs NS at day 9 (sleep restriction with equal training; paper: 0 DEGs, S3.2.p2)
final.normalization_filter: keep genes with at least 10 reads on average -> 15,543 transcripts (S2.8.p1)
final.paper_method: DESeq2 ("DESeq R package v1.40.2"; design formula not stated, pairing on participant not stated) (S2.8.p1)
final.paper_results: exercise contrasts ~3000 DEGs reported 'FDR < 0.05' in S3.2.p7 / S3.3.p2; sleep contrasts 1 and 0 DEGs; GSEA (fgsea, Reactome, log2FC ranking): oxidative metabolism up with training (S3.2.p8)

paper_reconstruction.reasoning: Methods S2.8.p1 states DESeq2 with padj < 0.05 and log2FC > 1 / < -1 on the mean>=10-reads filtered set. Results S3.2.p7 give exercise DEG counts labelled FDR < 0.05; S3.3.p2 gives the same counts (2834/2117 down, 129/102 up). The exercise estimand is a training/time contrast (day 9 pre vs day 3 pre) because only pre-exercise biopsies were sequenced (S2.7.p1).

checks: GEO treatment_protocol reproduces the paper's abstract design (10 females, 9 nights SR 5 h vs NS, REx days 3,5,7,9, biopsies days 3 and 9)
contact Danielle Hiam (Deakin IPAN) is an author
38 vastus lateralis female samples, treatment SLEEP/CON x day 3/9
filtered matrix size equals the paper's 15,543 transcripts

ownership.reasoning: GEO series metadata (treatment_protocol_ch1, contact) matches the paper ABS.p1 / S2.2 exactly; the gene count after the paper's filter reproduces S2.8.p1's 15,543.

alignment.reasoning: Matrix columns equal the GEO title (38/38). Title = 4-letter participant code + digit; digit 1/3/5/7 corresponds exactly to SLEEP-d3/SLEEP-d9/CON-d3/CON-d9 in the characteristics columns, so the participant key is the 4-letter prefix (10 participants). Condition and day come from the characteristics columns, not from the digit. Ages differ by one year between conditions for GEKN and KISZ, consistent with a cross-over spanning months.

matrix.matrix_type: estimated counts (Kallisto gene-level counts, deposited as integers)

final.source: GSE263838_GeneCounts_RAW_DATA.csv.gz filtered by prep/filter_mean10.py (mean count >= 10, 15,543 genes)

matrix.reasoning: Integer fraction 1.0, max 7.3e6, library sizes 23-29 M; data_processing says Kallisto transcript counts and 'aligned raw gene counts'. Kallisto estimates are non-integer, so the submitter already rounded/summed them to integer gene counts; this is the input the paper gave DESeq2. The 3col.tsv is the long-format copy of the same counts.

design.subject: subject

final.analysis_type: 2x2 factorial repeated measures (cell means), simple-effect contrasts

design.reasoning: Paper compares 'NS and SR conditions by day, as well as the same condition by day' (S2.8.p1) using all samples: four simple effects from one model. The exercise estimand is day 9 vs day 3 within each sleep condition; it combines three REx sessions with six more days in the condition and time-of-study, which the design cannot separate (no non-exercise arm), so it is labelled a training/time effect as the paper does. The cond x day interaction (does sleep restriction change the training response) is the paper's verbal claim (S3.3.p2) but it was argued from Euler overlaps, not tested; it runs as exploratory.

covariates.name: subject
covariates.disposition: blocking factor (participant; cross-over, 4 biopsies per woman)

covariates.name: age
covariates.disposition: not used: constant within participant, absorbed by subject

covariance.reasoning: Each participant contributes up to four samples (both conditions, both days): samples are not independent, so participant is a blocking term. The paper does not state its DESeq2 formula; an unblocked ~ grp fit runs as a sensitivity analysis to bracket the paper's counts. No sequencing batch is recorded. Estrogen/progesterone were tested and dropped by the paper (S2.12.p1) and are not deposited.

final.method: DESeq2 (pydeseq2 Wald), joint model on all 38 samples
deviations: participant blocking added (paper formula unstated); unblocked ~ grp run as sensitivity
counts were already integers as deposited; no further rounding applied (round on integers is the identity)

method.reasoning: Integer (rounded Kallisto) gene counts support DESeq2, the paper's method. The paper's low-count filter (mean >= 10 reads) is applied before fitting by prep/filter_mean10.py and reproduces its 15,543 genes exactly.

final.deviation_note: Methods (S2.8.p1) state padj < 0.05 and |log2FC| > 1; Results (S3.2.p7, S3.3.p2) label the exercise counts 'FDR < 0.05' only. The FDR-only rule is reported as the audit count so both readings can be compared.

threshold.reasoning: S2.8.p1: 'adjusted p-value of < 0.05 and Log2 fold change > 1 and <-1'; figure legends FIG1/FIG3 use the same two cutoffs.

caveats: Exercise contrast = day 9 pre-exercise vs day 3 pre-exercise: training effect confounded with time in the condition (no non-exercise arm); not an acute exercise response.
Paper DEG counts may use FDR only (Results) or FDR + |log2FC| > 1 (Methods); compare against both our applied and audit counts.
Participant blocking is our assumption; the paper's formula is unstated.
SASY contributes only SR day 3 and NS day 9 (SASY3 and SASY5 not deposited).

Paper totals are reproduced by the UNBLOCKED fit with FDR < 0.05 only (2965 vs 2962 NS; 2224 vs 2219 SR), so the paper's counts used FDR only (Results wording), not its Methods |log2FC| > 1 rule, and no participant blocking.

Paper's up/down split (128/2834 NS, 102/2117 SR) is not a sign split: its 'up' equals our padj < 0.05 and log2FC(D9/D3) < -1 (130 NS, 102 SR) and its 'down' equals the remaining FDR genes (2835, 2122). Our FDR-only sign split for D9 vs D3 is 1964 up / 1001 down (NS) and 1346 / 878 (SR).

Direction contradicts the paper's text: paper says oxidative metabolism is UP with training and cell cycle DOWN; our D9 vs D3 GSEA (Hallmark) has OXIDATIVE_PHOSPHORYLATION NES -2.57 (NS) / -2.58 (SR) and E2F/G2M NES +2.1 to +2.3. Paper's GGNBP2 is 'upregulated' by SR at day 3; ours log2FC(SR/NS) = -2.27. Both are consistent with the paper's contrasts being written reference-over-test (NS3_vs_NS9 = day 3 / day 9; NS3_vs_SR3 = NS / SR), i.e. the paper's stated directions are sign-reversed.
The cond x day interaction (exploratory) has 0 genes at FDR < 0.05: the 'moderating effect of sleep restriction' the paper infers from Euler overlaps is not supported by a formal interaction test.

study.reasoning: Counts from S3.2.p7 (128 up + 2834 down; 102 up + 2117 down) and S3.2.p2 (1 and 0).

executions.reasoning: Unblocked ~ cell, the likely paper formula (no pairing mentioned), to bracket the paper's DEG counts.

enrichment.reasoning: Paper ran fgsea ranked by log2FC on each contrast (S2.9.p2); our tool uses MSigDB Hallmark, not Reactome. Paper: oxidative metabolism up with training (S3.2.p8).
